reviews.title: Taxi Fare is Overpricing
reviews.text:
I am very disappointed with the response I received from your customer service regarding my taxi fare complaint.

I have been using Careem almost every day to commute to work, and this is the first time I have experienced a fare starting at AED 16.50 instead of the usual AED 13.50, despite booking the same Hala Taxi service that I always choose.

My usual fare for the same destination ranges from AED 29.50 to a maximum of AED 32.50, yet this time I was charged AED 42.50. This is a significant and unexpected increase, and I believe it deserves a proper explanation.

What disappoints me even more is the response I received from customer service, as I expected my concern to be taken seriously, especially as a regular customer. I am not satisfied with the response provided, and I would appreciate a clear explanation of why I was charged significantly more than my usual fare for the same journey.

As a loyal Careem customer, I expected better service and a more satisfactory resolution. I hope you will review this matter fairly and address my concern accordingly.

reviews.text:

The Careem captain was already physically at the restaurant, waited there for over an hour, communicated with me throughout and even put me on the phone with the kitchen to try to resolve it. He was the one person who actually seemed to be trying to help.

At around 8:26pm, Careem told me the issue was still being resolved. Moments later, they cancelled the order claiming “all our captains are busy” — despite my captain literally already being at the restaurant.

I then had to reorder dinner elsewhere and did not eat until around 9:15pm.

A Careem manager offered me AED 24 compensation that evening. I refused it because I thought it was insulting and raised a formal complaint. Astonishingly, Careem then changed its position and repeatedly told me that no compensation at all could be offered.

They also repeatedly ignored several points in my complaint, including whether the captain who lost more than an hour of his working time was compensated. I asked this multiple times and never received an answer.

I also requested cancellation and refund of my Careem Plus subscription after this experience, which was ignored too.

reviews.title: Profiting Off Customer Inconvenience
reviews.text:
I’ve had two bad experiences in a row with the Careem app, and it feels like the system is designed to profit from customer inconvenience rather than fix problems.

Two days ago, during a busy period, the Careem driver refused to pick up my order, yet I was still charged 2.5 JDs. What makes this worse is that this fee used to be 1.5 JDs, so the increase feels unjustified—especially when the issue was not my fault.

Today, I faced another problem. The driver stopped for a while because he didn’t receive my phone number. Instead of calling back or asking for the correct number, he simply waited, and I was then charged an extra 0.6 JDs. Charging that much for just two minutes of waiting, when a simple call could have solved the issue, is unreasonable.

These repeated incidents are frustrating and unfair. Customers shouldn’t be penalized for driver miscommunication or system errors. Unless this is addressed, it seriously affects my trust in the app.

Im in Salmiya and it shows him in Mahaboolah. I cancel the ride to find one in my city and I get hit with still having to pay the original 1 and then an additional 1 plus i have to cover for a new ride. But you cant get a new ride until you pay for the previous ride… “Even though he was more than 30 mins late”. How am i still being charged when the Driver is the one at fault…? I will be filing a complaint with the MOCI. Thats not proper business practice. I shouldn’t be charged for somebody else being late.
